rows.Light: Late afternoon, low sun across the grass; the porch light is already on and throws one long rectangle over tiles 4-6 of the near row.
rows.SoundBed: Wind in a chain-link fence, a screen door knocking in its frame, the robot's servo whine held at a steady clinical pitch.
rows.GateOpenMoment: The yard gate at the fence line unlatches and swings the moment the approach meter crosses 0.33; the checkpoint fires as the player steps through, keeping the meter and the four-move history.
rows.PlayerSees: Home ground turned into a ring. The robot dog stands between you and the house, head scanning for 600 ms every time you commit a step, and the porch light shows you exactly how much yard is left.
rows.NemesisPressure: Charge above 60 percent. It intercepts on the straight read of your last four moves and reports in a flat clinical register; it never sprints, so its pauses are rare and its predictions are its only weapon.

rows.Light: no house light past the gate, one neighbour's lamp on a motion timer that keeps guessing wrong
rows.SoundBed: chain link ringing whenever either animal touches it
Props: a chain link run between two yards
a gap dug under the bottom rail
a lamp pole with a dead sensor
rows.GateOpenMoment: at 66% the far panel is already down and the ground turns to ballast
rows.PlayerSees: The same shape of gap that took the back leg, with the machine standing in it.
rows.NemesisPressure: rising; it sprints once a phase and pays for it out of charge

rows.Light: sodium floods on tall poles, hard shadows that swing when nothing has moved
rows.SoundBed: an idling engine out of sight, couplings taking up slack one at a time
Props: a switch stand with its lamp lit
one boxcar with the door standing open
rows.GateOpenMoment: no gate; this phase ends the fight one way or the other
rows.PlayerSees: An open boxcar door, the same shape that saved the dog once, and this time the machine is in front of it.
rows.NemesisPressure: highest; charge is low, the reads are clipped, and it stops covering both exits

critic_findings.why: No canon beat id named limp_onset exists; the canon beat list is shelter escape, alley chase, freight-train leap, the coast through the boxcar door, the family's street, and the only literal id shown is "the_street" — "limping" appears in canon only as a dog_observable gait field, not as a beat.

critic_findings.span: the lit strip runs diagonally from tile [1,1] to tile [8,8] and is the only ground where the robot reads you cleanly
critic_findings.why: Canon gives the Nemesis unconditional perception every round ("you move → the Nemesis perceives your position + movement statistics", and dog_tile is always present in its input), so a lighting-gated perception is a new mechanic that contradicts the boss loop.

Canon's phase-2 payload (phase:2, approach_meter 0.6, which lands in this row's 0.33–0.66 band) lists cover_tiles [[3,5],[5,7]], and this row keeps [5,7] and canon's exits [0,6],[9,2] but drops [3,5], which the previous row has instead reassigned to phase 1.

critic_findings.span: Four covers, three exits, and a robot that pauses longer than it used to between reads.
critic_findings.why: This is the agent's tactical readout, not what the dog sees — canon puts the coarse tactical grid on the agent's side only, and the game's player-facing register is concrete sensory detail ("The porch light is the same. So is the shape moving behind the window"), not counted level entities.

critic_findings.span: the open boxcar door at [1,9] is the one bright rectangle on the board
critic_findings.why: "On the board" names the agent-side grid abstraction inside a scene description, breaking the fiction that the grid is overlaid for the agent rather than seen by the dog.

rows.Location: shelter yard, the gate seam between kennel run and open pavement
rows.PursuerType: shelter handler with a catch pole, fixed loop along the fence
rows.EscapeCondition: step through the gate seam on the turn after the pole swings, and cross the threshold onto pavement
rows.FailCondition: stand on the gate tile while the pole reaches it; the handler walks you back to the run and the loop restarts unchanged
rows.PlayerSees: The yard gate stands open a dog's width, and a man with a catch pole walks the fence on the same slow loop he has walked all morning. The pole tips left before it comes down, every pass. You wait out his turn, slip the gap, and the pavement keeps going further than the yard ever did.

rows.Location: service alley behind the row shops, dumpsters and stacked crates on both walls
rows.PursuerType: loose yard dog, same lunge pattern on every approach
rows.EscapeCondition: step off the lunge tile while the lunge commits right, then clear two corners
rows.FailCondition: share a tile with the lunge; a shoulder goes into the wall and the chase resets one block back
rows.PlayerSees: Something big comes off the wall behind you and leans right before it lunges, the same lean each time. You step off the tile it is coming to, let it commit to the empty side, and take the corner while it is still turning. Something gave up two corners ago. You keep running anyway.

rows.Location: four-lane arterial, curb to curb, no median
rows.PursuerType: moving traffic, obstacle not pursuer, lanes on a fixed cycle
rows.EscapeCondition: leave the curb on the beat after the horn and cross all four lanes in one unbroken line
rows.FailCondition: stop on a lane tile; horns and brakes push you back to the curb and the lane cycle repeats the same way
rows.PlayerSees: Four lanes, headlights stacked both directions, and nothing out here is chasing you. You read the space between the near truck and the next set of lights, and you take it in one line without stopping in the middle, because the middle is where the road decides for you.

rows.Location: rail yard gravel shoulder alongside a rolling freight
rows.PursuerType: yard patrol dog on the ballast, straight-line runner, no cutting
rows.EscapeCondition: match the car's speed on the shoulder and jump inside the two-turn window the open door gives you
rows.FailCondition: jump short of the door lip; you land on gravel, roll, and the freight takes the opening away
rows.PlayerSees: Gravel, a freight going faster than you are, and one boxcar door already yawning open. Behind you, paws on gravel. You pick the gap and you do not slow down for it, and the floor of the car comes up hard under your chest.

rows.Location: diner back lot, grease bins, chain fence on the far side, alley mouth behind
rows.PursuerType: kitchen hand at the screen door, same two-step out and back
rows.EscapeCondition: leave by the fence side while the door swings, or stay for the paper tray and leave by the fence side after
rows.FailCondition: back out through the alley mouth you came in by; you keep the food and lose the ground, and the yard runs the same two-step next time
rows.PlayerSees: The back door bangs and a hand you don't know puts down a paper tray. You can be gone before it straightens up, or you can eat first and decide about the hand after. Either way the yard has two ways out, and only one of them is forward.

rows.Location: chain link fence line at the lot edge, a scraped hollow under the wire
rows.PursuerType: loose dog off the lot, three-tile sweep it has run on every approach, never varied
rows.EscapeCondition: reach the hollow and go under while the sweep is on its left tile, one clear tile of space between you
rows.FailCondition: take the hollow with the sweep adjacent; the wire and the teeth arrive together and the crossing costs you the rest of the day
rows.PlayerSees: Chain link, a scraped hollow under it, and the thing behind you close enough that you hear it set its feet. It drops the same shoulder it has dropped on every pass. You go under, the wire takes the back leg on the way through, and the back leg has opinions now. You tell it what you told the gate: not yet.

critic_findings.why: Canon defines the Act 3 boss fight only as tile-step-and-telegraph grammar on a coarse tactical grid with predicted_tile/intercept_move, so cover and the row's "break line of sight behind a dumpster" name a system Act 3 does not have.

critic_findings.span: Through the open door, later, the coast.
critic_findings.why: Canon places "the coast seen through the open boxcar door" after the freight-train leap, so this hazard's day-3 narration states a fact dated later than its own day.
Act 3 is a pursuit-evasion boss fight in a compact sealed arena run on the tile-step-and-telegraph grammar; choosing between two ways out of a yard is not a mechanic that exists there.

critic_findings.span: three-tile sweep it has run since the shelter road, never varied

critic_findings.span: It drops the same shoulder it has dropped all week.
critic_findings.why: Same contradiction stated in-fiction: it asserts a week of identical behavior from a pursuer whose canonical telegraph on this journey is the opposite-side lunge.

critic_findings.why: The machine's memory is a 4-move sliding window and its only non-decaying statistics are direction frequency over 20 moves and a periodicity score, so a five-round record of which tiles the target ended on is knowledge it cannot hold.

The read names the internal engine-computed scalar and its cutoff instead of leading with the behavior, and the second clause already states the behavior, so the abstraction is both drift and redundant.
Sixty percent is the boundary between the clinical and confident bands, so a line reporting that charge has already crossed it cannot be delivered in the clinical register this row is tagged with.

The diagnosis half is clean, but 'Sealed.' declares the left route closed for the move the player has not yet committed, which is the read-line oracle announcing the plan rather than past-tense diagnosis only.
One move per round means five rounds of ending tiles is memory beyond the machine's 4-move sliding window, and the non-decaying statistics are only direction frequency and periodicity.

critic_findings.span: You ended three of five rounds behind cover.
critic_findings.why: The cited observable cover_tiles is a list of current cover positions and carries no record of where the dog ended prior rounds, so the line asserts more than the observable supports.
The cited observable is a single periodicity scalar (0.72) that reports how cyclic the movement is, not the cycle length, so the machine cannot name the period as five beats.
Counting a five-beat loop requires move history longer than the 4-move sliding window the machine is canonically limited to.

Counting three cover-endings across the last five rounds exceeds what the machine retains: its move memory is a 4-move sliding window and the only non-decaying data are the engine scalars dir_freq_20 and periodicity, neither of which tracks cover-tile endings.

Speed is not an observable the Nemesis receives — dog_observable carries only gait and collar — and canon fixed movement as equal speed with the 2-tile sprint belonging to the robot, so a drop in the dog's speed is an inference the machine cannot make from its input.
The charge band is the register the read is spoken in (clinical/confident/strained), not content the robot announces; naming the band states the strain the player is supposed to hear in the voice.
